Read IN FULL: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev/646bc8ac-afb6-41b4-8d24-dcbaf28144cd/scratchpad/turns_chunk03.txt

This file contains every user turn Marcel Navarro typed across ~24 Claude Code sessions while working as FED Lead on the Zimmermann PWA Kit (a Salesforce PWA Kit / React / Chakra codebase). Sessions are separated by `====` lines with a `### [tag] [date] Title — N user turns` header. Turns are marked `--- turn N ---`.

READ THE WHOLE FILE. It is large (~478,000 tokens), so read it in sequential slices using Read with offset/limit. Maintain a running findings list as you go and DISCARD raw text after each slice — never try to hold the whole file in context.

We are designing personal workflow skills for Marcel. The transcripts are the evidence for WHY those skills are needed. Extract these six things:

**1. RECURRING CORRECTIONS — the highest priority.**
Places where Marcel had to re-state an established way of working that had been ignored or got wrong. He has said he had to "stress again and again" the set approach. Find those. For each, give: verbatim quote (trimmed to the relevant sentences), the session title, turn number, and tag it with the area:
`overriding` | `tokens` | `components` | `atomic-design` (atoms/molecules/organisms) | `css-structure` | `css-strategy` | `tests` | `stories` | `a11y` | `typescript` | `contentful` | `scope` | `git/branching` | `other`
Count how many DISTINCT times each area comes up. That count is the single most important output.

**2. DESIGN CONFORMANCE.**
Where he had to check or re-check that a build matched the Figma design — variants, states, tokens, viewports, spacing. Quote the checks he actually performs and what he looks for.

**3. FRUSTRATION / RE-WORK SIGNALS.**
Turns containing corrections: "again", "I said", "no —", "that's not", "you missed", "why did you", "revert", "you were supposed to", "as I mentioned". These mark where the workflow broke down. Quote and categorise.

**4. WHAT WORKED.**
Successes. Especially any use of a closed-loop / multi-agent / orchestrator-builder-tester-scorer workflow. Quote how he set it up and what he said about the result. Also note any prompt pattern he reused because it worked.

**5. HIS PROMPT FORMULAS.**
Recurring phrasings and structures he types — the shape of his asks. We want to encode his voice and method into skills, so capture the actual language, not a paraphrase.

**6. REVIEW-MODE BEHAVIOUR.**
He is also senior dev / reviewer. Where he reviews others' PRs or code, capture: what he checks, in what order, what he rejects, and how he phrases feedback.

OUTPUT: a structured report with these six sections. Lead section 1 with a frequency table of areas. Use verbatim quotes throughout — quotes are the deliverable, not summaries. Be concrete. If a section has nothing, say so explicitly.

985	
986	Structured by tier, per the team's approach: atoms compose into molecules, styling lives in theme
987	recipes, and we override rather than rebuild so we inherit existing wiring.

989	**Atoms** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<camelCase>/`, each `index.tsx` +
990	`index.stories.tsx`:
991	
992	| Atom | Spec | Recipe? |
993	|---|---|---|
994	| `zimmProductName` | `textStyle="heading3"` | No — tiers 1–2 cover it |
995	| `zimmProductPrice` | `textStyle="price"` | **Yes** — `default` now; `sale` is the extension point SFCC-194 needs (`pdp/price` has both states) |
996	| `zimmProductDescription` | sanitised HTML, `textStyle="body2"` | **Yes** — responsive mobile inset |
997	| `zimmProductModelInfo` | `textStyle="caption"` | No — tiers 1–2 cover it |
998	| `zimmProductStyleCode` | label + value, `textStyle="caption"` | **Yes** — multipart; the DS models it as two nodes (label 57px at x=0, value 157px at x=61) |

1001	the DS's own `Content` frame (218×82). Its recipe carries the 20px internal rhythm and the

1005	them at the bottom after the accordions rather than with the description.

1052	resolvers, unit-test it there, let Storybook `play` drive the component. `AGENTS.md:151`,
1053	`code-quality/SKILL.md:95` and `new-component/SKILL.md:50` all permit `.test.ts` **or** `play`, and
1054	Storybook interaction + a11y are **required checks** on `develop`, so a play-only component is

1059	| # | Gap | What we do |
1060	|---|---|---|
1061	| G1 | Nothing ties external data shape to props. A mis-keyed field falls to `?? ''` and renders empty — invisible to `play` and to axe. `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product→props mapping: every field, including absent, asserting the right field reached the right prop. |
1062	| G2 | Nothing asserts a recipe's declared `parts` match what the component *reads*. Drift ⇒ `__css={undefined}` ⇒ silently unstyled. | Assert `parts` ⊇ the part names the component consumes. Comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys is insufficient — renaming both stays green. |
1063	| G3 | Props crossing composition boundaries are unchecked. | Assert any prop crossing more than one boundary reaches the leaf. |
1064	| G4 | Vacuity — suites asserting "no offenders" pass on empty input. Only `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards this. | Any such suite of ours carries a self-test proving it collected something. Copy `recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174`. |
1065	| G5 | #59 asserts focus-trap behaviour in both a hook test and a `play`, against `testing.md:3`. | One layer per behaviour; note the choice. |
1066	| G6 | A skipped required check satisfies branch protection. Correct when only docs/tooling changed; a hole when source changed. | Before requesting review, verify the gates ran on **the last commit that touched testable source**, not merely on head. |

7179	As a Shopper, 
7180	I want to see a consistent global footer on every page, 
7181	so that I can access navigation links, contact information, legal content, and newsletter sign-up from anywhere on the site.
7182	
7183	Reference image (Figma is leading):
7184	
7185	image-20260618-041717.png
7186	The global footer is displayed at the bottom of every page across all storefronts and devices. It is CMS-managed via Contentful, allowing business users to update footer links and copy without a code deployment. The content of the footer (e.g. links) can be configured per storefront. Contentful integration is covered in a separate user story. This story covers the footer shell, layout, and component structure only — footer link destinations, email sign-up Omneo integration, and Cookie Settings behaviour are covered in separate stories.

# MARCEL NAVARRO — WORKFLOW EVIDENCE REPORT (turns_chunk03)

**Corpus:** 24 sessions, 2026-07-19 → 2026-08-29, 926 user turns. Dominated by one session — `[pwa] [2026-08-28] ZIMM - PR #55` (591 turns, the SFCC-55 global footer build) — which is where nearly all build-discipline evidence lives. Second-densest: `[pwa] [2026-08-13] ZIMM - SFCC-237` (78 turns, spike TSD) and `[pwa] [2026-08-25] SFCC - PR #57` (60 turns, PDP plan).

---

## 1. RECURRING CORRECTIONS — FREQUENCY TABLE

Counted as **distinct occasions** where Marcel re-states an established way of working that was ignored, missed, or got wrong. Verbatim restatements of the same sentence in consecutive turns are counted separately **only where the restatement is itself the signal** (i.e. he had to say it again because it didn't land).

| Rank | Area | Distinct occasions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`other` → design conformance vs Figma** | **~45** | The single largest cluster by a wide margin. Broken out fully in §2. |
| **2** | **`scope`** | **~38** | "out of scope stays out of scope", over-delivery, over-engineering, unauthorised edits |
| **3** | **`git/branching`** | **~26** | Commit granularity, PR body standards, no Claude attribution, no commit without go-signal |
| **4** | **`tests`** | **~18** | "actual tests ran against it?", proof-not-assertion, phase suite |
| **5** | **`css-structure`** | **~15** | The "components, tokens, and css structure" triad — restated near-verbatim ~12 times |
| **5=** | **`tokens`** | **~15** | Correct token in use, provisional/local tokens, literals vs vars |
| **7** | **`stories`** | **~12** | Storybook as a mandatory build artefact and a visual-check surface |
| **8** | **`atomic-design`** | **~11** | Atom/molecule/organism completeness — "all variants and states" |
| **9** | **`css-strategy`** | **~14** | No inline, no hardcoded, no mirrored styles; hierarchy adherence |
| **10** | **`components`** | **~11** | Override-first, don't rebuild, don't duplicate |
| **11** | **`contentful`** | **~9** | Fixture vs live data, env provisioning |
| **12** | **`a11y`** | **~8** | Perceivable-but-inert, target size, new-tab announcement |

| **14** | **`typescript`** | **~5** | Lowest. Mostly delegated to the `code-quality` skill's Agent C |

## 4. WHAT WORKED

### 4a. The closed-loop multi-agent workflow — his invention, stated in full

This is the highest-value artefact in the corpus. He designed it himself, unprompted, at *SFCC - PR #57* turn 11 (repeated at 12 and 15 with only small edits):

> **"we utilize and execute a closed-loop agent workflow that will involve 5 agents: - first an agent that will look at the updated dev docs at [4 playbook paths] - next, an agent that will look into the changes/implementations that the latest and latest merged PR @ PR #59 which is now in develop sets/establishes as part of the footer UI build - next, an agent that will look into the current implementation/build that we have on this branch particularly how we've approached this so far and the implementation that we've put in place - next, an agent that will execute an in-depth analysis and comparison between the findings of [those two] - next, an agent that will score and check the findings to make sure they are accurate and have factual basis - next, an agent that will take everything and create an up-to-date revised plan of attack which will then in turn use the scorer and checker agent to verify the plan - and finally, an agent that will run feasibility checking and testing on the proposed and verified plan - what do you think of my plan?"**

Turn 12 changes the ending to **"do not execute anything yet, let's go over the plan first and align on it"**; turn 15 to **"do not execute anything yet, let's go over the plan first to sanity test and align on it"**.

**His verdict on the result:**
> **"that was one hell of a back-and-forth since the closed-loop workflow with 8 agent invocations, 6 types, and 1 revision round was concluded - we now have a revised and updated plan, what's our confidence on the current state of the plan compared to the closed-loop workflow's plan?"**
> — *SFCC - PR #57*, turn 59

> **"i want the level of scrutiny and certainty an eight-agent loop is able to provide but i know that's overkill so help me plan for a closed-loop multi-agent workflow scaled down to what we actually need to have the confidence in the plan that we have in place"**
> — *SFCC - PR #57*, turn 60 — **this is the design brief for a skill.**

### 6b. Order of checks (as practised)

1. **Sync first.** "make sure we have all branches from github remote in local and that all active branches are up to date" (typed at the start of 4 different sessions); pull the PR branch locally — "**pull the PRs (their branches) locally with the latest and review and test locally**".

4. **Against the ticket.** "let's run the code against the jira ticket details"; "here's the ticket for the footer: [full Jira paste] - **what does this tell us about the clearance?**"

6. **Mechanical gates.** phase 0–6 suite, `code-quality` skill, local CodeRabbit.
7. **Adversarial re-pass.** "**do another audit across all 3 PRs to challenge, confirm, and validate the verdicts**"; "**perform another complete/deep check/audit - the Tier-1 Approvers are unsure/skeptical of this PR**"; "**what was the difference with the previous and this new review pass? why was it given the go-signal on the previous and changes requested on this recent review pass?**"
